dimensions.evidence: Issue titles are bold white text with coloured label pills next to them, and the rows are divided by thin separators. The blue 'New Issue' button stands out at the top right. The search bar, the Labels/Milestones buttons and the filter row line up on one grid. Below the 4 issues, roughly 40% of the viewport is empty.
dimensions.justification: The grouping and F-pattern flow are clear: search, then state tabs and filters, then the list. The filter dropdowns are right-aligned and far from the Open/Closed toggle, so the user's eye has to cross a wide empty gap. This is a minor issue.

dimensions.evidence: The repo header (Code, Issues 4, Pull Requests…), the Open/Closed toggle, the label pills, the '#3 opened now by judge-demo' metadata and the dropdown carets all follow GitHub/Gitea conventions. Icons are used consistently in both the tabs and the state toggle.
dimensions.justification: The view matches standard Git platform patterns closely, and its components are uniform throughout.

dimensions.evidence: The 'Issues' tab is underlined and shows the counter 4. The '4 Open' segment is highlighted next to '1 Closed'. The breadcrumb reads 'judge-demo / web-shop'. Each row has an open-state icon.
dimensions.justification: Location and object states are clear. However, the active state of '4 Open' is only a slightly lighter background, and nothing shows which filters are active (for example, no chip says 'Label: bug' or 'no filter'). Disabled Milestone/Project dropdowns give no reason for being disabled.

dimensions.evidence: The labels are short and familiar: 'Labels', 'Milestones', 'New Issue', 'Author', 'Assignee', 'Type', 'Sort'. Issue titles are descriptive, e.g. 'Error 500 on empty search'.
dimensions.justification: Wording is clear overall. The search placeholder 'Search...' doesn't say what is searched or whether filter syntax is supported. 'Labels' and 'Milestones' appear both as buttons and as dropdowns, which could confuse new users about the difference between managing and filtering.

dimensions.evidence: Milestone and Project dropdowns are greyed out, which stops users choosing empty filters. Row checkboxes for bulk actions are shown, but no destructive action is visible until a row is selected.
dimensions.justification: This view has few risky actions. Disabling empty filters prevents dead ends, but no tooltip explains why they are disabled. Bulk-action behaviour can't be assessed from the screenshot.

dimensions.evidence: The 'Label' dropdown filter sits in the filter bar, and the default view already shows open issues. Search, Author, Assignee and Sort filters are all visible without extra steps. The 'bug' pills on #3 and #1 are easy to recognise.
dimensions.justification: Finding open bugs takes 2 clicks (Label, then bug), or the user can just scan this short list. With more issues, it's unclear whether clicking a label pill filters the list. There are no saved or quick filters such as 'bugs'.

dimensions.evidence: Each row shows only the state icon, title, label, number, time and author. There are no avatars, comment counters or decoration competing with the content. The footer holds technical data (Page: 63ms, Template: 4ms) in small text.
dimensions.justification: Information density suits the task, and the screen has no superfluous elements. The footer timing information is unobtrusive.

dimensions.evidence: The grey metadata text '#5 opened now by judge-demo' and the 'Search...' placeholder are low-contrast grey on a near-black background. The disabled 'Milestone'/'Project' text is very dim. The white text on the bright green 'enhancement' pill is small (~11px) and likely below 4.5:1. Row checkboxes are ~14px, which is close to the 24px target-size minimum. The open-state icons and the selected '4 Open' segment rely on subtle colour and shade differences.
dimensions.justification: Titles are clearly legible. Several pieces of secondary text and small controls are likely to fall short of WCAG 1.4.3 (contrast) and 2.5.8 (target size). Contrast can only be estimated from the screenshot.

strengths: The layout follows familiar GitHub-style conventions: state toggle, filter dropdowns and coloured label pills.
A clean, minimal issue list where titles and labels are scannable at a glance.
The Issues tab, its counter and the Open/Closed counts clearly show where the user is and what state the issues are in.

recommendations.recommendation: Raise the contrast of secondary metadata text, the search placeholder and the white-on-green label text to at least 4.5:1. Enlarge the row checkboxes, or their hit area, to 24×24px.
Show active filters as removable chips (e.g. 'Label: bug ×') and make the selected Open/Closed segment more visually distinct.
Make the label pills in rows visibly clickable so they filter the list, and consider quick filters such as 'Open bugs' next to the state toggle.
Add tooltips to the disabled Milestone/Project dropdowns explaining why they are disabled (e.g. 'No milestones in this repository').
Use a more specific search placeholder, e.g. 'Search issues by title or content…'.

dimensions.evidence: The issue titles are bold and white, and their metadata ('#3 opened now by judge-demo') is smaller grey text underneath. The blue 'New Issue' button is the only filled button, top right. The toolbar is in two rows: search, Labels, Milestones and New Issue on the first, and the Open/Closed toggle plus the filter dropdowns on the second. Rows are separated by thin dividers.
dimensions.justification: Grouping and alignment are clear, and the list scans well from top to bottom. The weak point is that the filter dropdowns sit far to the right, away from the list on the left, and about 40% of the viewport below the 4 issues is empty space. Neither problem gets in the way of the task.

dimensions.evidence: The repo tabs (Code, Issues 4, Pull Requests…) all use an icon plus a label. Labels use the same pill style throughout ('bug' red, 'enhancement' green). Every open issue has the same green circle icon. The Open/Closed toggle, the filter dropdowns with carets and Watch/Star/Fork with counters all follow GitHub/GitLab conventions.
dimensions.justification: Components, icons and colours are consistent within the view and match common Git platform patterns.

dimensions.evidence: The 'Issues' tab is underlined and has a count of 4. The '4 Open' toggle is highlighted, while '1 Closed' is not. The breadcrumb 'judge-demo / web-shop' is visible. Disabled filters ('Milestone', 'Project') are shown greyed out.
dimensions.justification: It is clear where the user is and that open issues are showing. However, an active filter is not shown anywhere except through the toggle. A label filter would only show up inside its dropdown, and the search field's placeholder doesn't state the current query. There is also no explanation of why Milestone and Project are disabled (presumably there are none).

dimensions.evidence: Labels are short and clear: 'New Issue', 'Label', 'Author', 'Assignee', 'Sort', '4 Open', '1 Closed'. The metadata reads 'opened now by judge-demo'. The search placeholder is just 'Search...'.
dimensions.justification: Wording is plain and fits the domain. 'Search...' doesn't say what is searched (titles? content?) or that filter syntax is supported. Having both 'Labels' (a management button) and 'Label' (a filter) next to each other could confuse some users.

dimensions.evidence: Milestone and Project, which have no options, are disabled and can't be clicked. There are no destructive actions in the view. The bulk-select checkboxes don't yet show any bulk actions.
dimensions.justification: This is a read and filter view with little risk of error. Disabling empty filters prevents dead-end clicks. Whether bulk actions such as close ask for confirmation can't be seen.

dimensions.evidence: Open issues are filtered by default. The 'Label' dropdown is right on the toolbar, and the red 'bug' pills are visible on issues #3 and #1, so they can be spotted at a glance. There is a search field and a Sort control.
dimensions.justification: Finding open bugs takes one or two clicks, or none with only 4 issues. Clicking a label pill to filter by it is common on Git platforms, but whether it works here can't be seen. No saved or quick filter such as 'label:bug' is visible.

dimensions.evidence: Each row shows only the state icon, title, labels, number, age and author. The top area has three rows of navigation (global nav, repo header with Watch/Star/Fork and repo tabs) before the list starts. The footer shows 'Page: 63ms Template: 4ms'.
dimensions.justification: The content is focused and uncluttered. Technical timing data in the footer doesn't help users, and the stack of navigation rows is heavy, but this is all standard and doesn't distract much.

dimensions.evidence: The disabled 'Milestone' and 'Project' filters are very low-contrast grey on near-black. The metadata text ('#5 opened now by judge-demo') is mid-grey and small, about 13px. The label pills have small white text (about 11px) on bright green or red. Open/closed state relies on a thin green circle icon. The row checkboxes and the counter badges in the tabs are small.
dimensions.justification: The main text is legible. However, the small white text on the green 'enhancement' pill is probably close to or below 4.5:1. Distinguishing bugs relies mainly on colour, although the text on the pill helps. The disabled filters are hard to read, and the checkbox targets look close to the 24px minimum. These problems would slow down users with low vision.

strengths: The labels are shown as coloured, readable pills right next to each title, so open bugs can be picked out at a glance.
Standard Git platform patterns: an Open/Closed toggle with counts, a filter bar with dropdowns, and an active-tab underline with an issue counter.
The list rows are clean and only show what's needed (title, label, number, author, age).

recommendations.recommendation: Increase the label pill text size (12px or more) and check that the white-on-green and white-on-red contrast is at least 4.5:1, for example by darkening the green. Lighten the disabled filters and the metadata text so they meet the 4.5:1 or 3:1 thresholds.
Show active filters as removable chips above the list (e.g. 'Label: bug ×'), or put the query in the search field (e.g. 'is:open label:bug'), so the current filtered state is always visible.
Make the label pills in the list clickable shortcuts that filter by that label. Offer a quick filter or a search syntax hint for common queries such as open bugs.
Make the search placeholder more specific (e.g. 'Search issues by title or content…'), and rename the 'Labels' button to 'Manage labels' so it isn't confused with the 'Label' filter.
Hide the server timing details ('Page: 63ms Template: 4ms') from regular users, and add a tooltip explaining why Milestone and Project are disabled.

dimensions.evidence: The issue titles are bold and white, so they are the main thing you see. The blue 'New Issue' button at the top right stands out as the main action. The filter bar (Label, Milestone, Project, Author, Assignee, Type, Sort) sits in a single row above the list. List rows are separated by thin dividers with even spacing.
dimensions.justification: The layout is clear and easy to scan from the top left. One small issue: the filter dropdowns float to the right, well away from the Open/Closed toggle, which leaves a big empty gap in the middle. The lower half of the viewport is also empty, but that is because there are only four issues.

dimensions.evidence: The tab bar (Code, Issues 4, Pull Requests, Actions…), the '4 Open / 1 Closed' toggle, the coloured label pills and the '#N opened now by user' metadata all follow GitHub/GitLab conventions. Icons are used the same way throughout: an open-circle icon for open issues and a tag icon for Labels.
dimensions.justification: Components and wording match common Git platform standards and are consistent within the app.

dimensions.evidence: The 'Issues' tab is underlined and shows a counter of 4. The breadcrumb 'judge-demo / web-shop' shows which repository you are in. The '4 Open' toggle is highlighted and '1 Closed' shows the other count. Each issue has a green open-state icon.
dimensions.justification: It is clear where you are and what state the issues are in. However, the 'Open' toggle is only slightly highlighted (dark grey on dark), and there is no visible summary of which filters are active. Milestone and Project look disabled, but nothing explains why.

dimensions.evidence: The labels 'Labels', 'Milestones', 'New Issue', 'Author', 'Assignee' and 'Sort' are plain. Issue titles are descriptive, and 'opened now by judge-demo' reads naturally.
dimensions.justification: The wording is clear overall. 'Type' is vague about what it filters, and the search box only says 'Search…' without saying what can be searched (titles, content, numbers).

dimensions.evidence: Checkboxes for selecting issues are shown, but no bulk actions appear until something is selected. Milestone and Project are greyed out instead of offering options that would return nothing.
dimensions.justification: There is little risk of mistakes on this read-only list. Greying out unavailable filters helps prevent dead ends, though it is not explained. Bulk actions behind the checkboxes could not be checked from the screenshot.

dimensions.evidence: To find open bugs, the user has to open the 'Label' dropdown and pick 'bug', or scan the red 'bug' pills by eye. The pills on the rows (#3, #1) may be clickable, but nothing shows that. There are no saved or quick filters such as 'bug' chips.
dimensions.justification: The task takes two clicks plus the default Open state, which is reasonable. But nothing visible suggests that clicking a label pill filters the list, and there is no quick label shortcut. With a longer list, scanning would be slow.

dimensions.evidence: Each row shows only the state icon, title, labels, number, age and author. There are no extra banners. The footer is small and out of the way.
dimensions.justification: The amount of information fits the task well, and nothing unnecessary competes for attention.

dimensions.evidence: The metadata text ('#5 opened now by judge-demo') is small grey text on a near-black background. The label pills use small white bold text on bright red/green. The disabled Milestone/Project text has very low contrast. Checkboxes are about 13px, below the 24px target size. Open/closed state is shown by icon shape as well as colour, which is good.
dimensions.justification: The secondary text and small checkboxes may not meet WCAG 1.4.3 contrast and 2.5.8 target size. Label meaning depends partly on colour, but the text inside the pills reduces that problem.

strengths: Follows familiar Git platform conventions: Open/Closed toggle with counts, coloured label pills, '#N opened by' metadata
A clean, uncluttered list where issue titles and labels stand out
Filters and search are all available in one toolbar above the list

recommendations.recommendation: Increase the contrast of the grey metadata text and disabled filter labels to at least 4.5:1, and make the row checkboxes at least 24×24px.
Make it visible that label pills can be clicked to filter (cursor/underline or tooltip 'Filter by bug'), and add quick-filter chips for frequently used labels such as 'bug'.

Show active filters as removable chips above the list and highlight the selected Open/Closed toggle more strongly. Add a tooltip explaining why Milestone/Project are disabled (e.g. 'No milestones yet').
Make the search placeholder more specific (e.g. 'Search issues by title, content or #number') and rename 'Type' to something more descriptive.
